correctness.rationale: The conference identity A^2=tI-A+tJ yields exactly three Laplacian eigenvalues. Rational interpolation yields a common strictly positive denominator and explicit entry numerators. Adjacent and nonadjacent entries are positive for all h>0. The diagonal quartic is positive for t=1,2; for each t>=3 it is positive at 0 and infinity, negative at h=2, and has at most two positive zeros by Descartes sign count. Therefore its two roots are simple and delimit exactly one negative interval. Fixed-scale limits of the quartic prove both asymptotics. Direct exact rational replay confirms 40 inverse matrices and 11,240 entry identities, without standing in for the general proof.

value.rationale: Conference graphs are a natural two-point correlation class, including an infinite Paley family. The result pinpoints the first attained graph size at which a widely used L-stable integrator loses the heat-flow maximum principle, describes the complete allowed timesteps rather than just a sufficient CFL condition, proves positivity of every distinct-vertex transition, and yields two different sharp timestep asymptotics.
